notes.2: First pass: walk the arguments to compute the total length needed.
notes.3: Adds each argument's length plus one (for a separator).
notes.4: Allocates exactly that many bytes for the concatenated arguments.
notes.6: Second pass: copy each argument into the buffer, unescaping as it goes.
notes.7: Loop over the characters of the current argument until the NUL.
notes.8: If this char is a backslash and the next is not whitespace, treat it as an escape.
notes.9: Skip the backslash so the escaped character is copied literally.
notes.10: Copy one character and advance both pointers.
notes.12: Write a space after each argument.

options.label: `malloc(size)` is not checked for NULL, so a failed allocation is dereferenced
options.whyWrong: Allocation failure is a separate, lesser issue; the exploited bug is the write past the buffer.

options.label: When an argument ends in a lone backslash, line 8 is true, line 9 skips it, then line 10 copies the terminating NUL and advances past the end — so the inner loop keeps reading and writing attacker bytes beyond `user_args`
`isspace()` with a signed char is undefined for negative values
options.whyWrong: The `(unsigned char)` cast already guards that; it is not the root cause here.

options.label: Allocate size * 2 to leave head-room
options.whyWrong: The read/write is unbounded once the loop runs off the string; a bigger buffer only moves the overflow.

options.label: Only treat a backslash as an escape when a character actually follows it
Replace the manual loop with strncpy(to, from, size)
options.whyWrong: This drops the unescaping entirely and still trusts a length that the escape logic made wrong; it doesn't address the over-read.

training.exploit: Invoke sudo in a mode that reaches this path (e.g. `sudoedit -s`) with an argument ending in a single backslash followed by a long attacker-controlled string. The escape handling walks past the end of the argument and copies attacker bytes beyond `user_args` on the heap, corrupting adjacent allocator metadata — crafted carefully, this yields local root.

hints.line: The copy overflows, but the faulty decision is the escape test above it.
hints.bugClass: Memory is written past the end of a heap buffer.
hints.why: What happens when `from` points at a backslash that is the last character?
hints.fix: Don't treat a trailing backslash as escaping the NUL terminator.

writeup.summary: In shell/edit mode, sudo copied the command line into a heap buffer while unescaping backslashes. The escape test checked `from[1]` without first confirming a character exists: for an argument ending in a lone `\`, it skipped the backslash and copied the terminating NUL, then the `while (*from)` loop continued reading and writing past the end of the argument — a heap buffer overflow with attacker-controlled contents. Because sudo is setuid root and the path is reachable without a password prompt in that mode, it became a reliable local privilege escalation (Baron Samedit). The fix stops treating a trailing backslash as an escape.
